input.description: A sustainable activewear brand for women. Made from recycled ocean plastic. Price point sits between Lululemon and Girlfriend Collective.

brief.statusReason: The advertiser clearly describes selling sustainable women's activewear made from recycled ocean plastic with specific price benchmarks.
brief.productSummary: Sustainable women's activewear made from recycled ocean plastic, positioned at a premium price point.
assumptions: Assumed a typical single order value of approximately $90 USD based on being positioned between Lululemon and Girlfriend Collective.
Assumed a standard one-time e-commerce purchase model.

persona.name: The Wellness Optimizer
persona.description: Tracks sleep, supplements, and workouts. Treats her body like a system to optimize. Willing to pay premiums for evidence-backed products.

reasons.label: low price sensitivity vs premium pricing

persona.name: The Fitness Enthusiast
persona.description: Works out 4+ times a week, follows fitness creators, buys performance apparel and supplements. Brand-loyal to things that perform. Identity-adjacent purchasing.

reasons.label: low-medium price sensitivity vs premium pricing

persona.name: The Affluent Classic
persona.description: Established career or retired, disposable income, values quality and longevity over trends. Shops less frequently but at higher AOVs. Loyal to brands she trusts.

reasons.label: low price sensitivity vs premium pricing

persona.name: The Gifter
persona.description: Not a persistent persona so much as a mode: any shopper within 30 days of a gifting holiday or life event. Higher AOV, looking for 'impressive-looking' purchases. Very responsive to gift-wrap and gifting messaging.

reasons.label: low price sensitivity vs premium pricing

persona.name: The Gen Z Aesthete
persona.description: Highly visual, identity-expressive buyer. Discovers through TikTok and Instagram. Cares about brand voice, packaging, and whether the brand stands for something.

reasons.label: medium-high price sensitivity vs premium pricing

persona.name: The Pet Parent
persona.description: Treats their pet as a family member. Reads ingredient labels on pet food. Will pay a premium for health and quality. Often owns multiple pets.

reasons.label: low-medium price sensitivity vs premium pricing

persona.name: The Sustainability Buyer
persona.description: Makes purchase decisions based on environmental and ethical footprint. Researches supply chains. Will pay more for genuinely sustainable options and is skeptical of greenwashing.

persona.name: The Busy Parent
persona.description: Dual-income household with kids. Time-poor, convenience-motivated. Buys in bulk, loves subscriptions, trusts brands that have been recommended by other parents.

persona.name: The Convenience-First Millennial
persona.description: Urban, mid-to-high income, values speed and frictionlessness. Default to what's easy. Heavy subscription user. Low brand loyalty if another option is just as convenient.

persona.name: The Value-Conscious Shopper
persona.description: Budget-aware but not low-end. Looks for deals, reads reviews, comparison shops. Responds well to bundles, first-order discounts, and clear value articulation.

reasons.label: high price sensitivity vs premium pricing

publisher.name: Movewell
publisher.notes: Fitness-engaged shoppers. Strong crossover with wellness and beauty.

reasons.label: Shopped by The Wellness Optimizer, The Fitness Enthusiast, The Affluent Classic

publishers.rationale: This publisher is a superb match given its highly fitness-engaged, 82% female audience who frequently shop both activewear and wellness categories. Your premium recycled ocean plastic messaging will resonate deeply with this group.
publishers.concern: The presence of a subscription subcategory indicates customers might expect recurring purchase benefits or bundles.

publisher.name: Cloudfoot
publisher.notes: Tech-adjacent urban professionals. Comfort + sustainability messaging.

reasons.label: Shopped by The Wellness Optimizer, The Fitness Enthusiast

publishers.rationale: Their audience actively responds to sustainability messaging and has a mid-to-high income level that easily supports a 90 dollar price point.
publishers.concern: The balanced gender split means nearly half of your ad spend will reach males for a female-focused activewear line.

publisher.name: Stride & Stem
publisher.notes: Professional women. Sustainability and machine-washable claims resonate.

reasons.label: Shopped by The Fitness Enthusiast, The Affluent Classic

publishers.rationale: An affluent, 94% female audience that prioritizes both sustainability claims and premium apparel provides a highly receptive, high-intent pool of prospective buyers.
publishers.concern: Because their primary apparel focus is footwear, your creative assets must clearly position your activewear offerings.

publisher.name: Studiogrid
publisher.notes: Appointment-based booking. Users are actively spending on self-care and fitness.

reasons.label: Shopped by The Wellness Optimizer, The Fitness Enthusiast
Price is 2.1× this audience's typical $42 order

publishers.rationale: Users here are actively spending high incomes on yoga, fitness classes, and wellness services, making them the absolute ideal target market for sustainable activewear. The automated rules incorrectly penalized this platform based on booking fees rather than overall retail purchasing power.
publishers.concern: The platform is focused on appointment bookings rather than traditional e-commerce browsing.

publisher.name: Pantrygood
publisher.notes: Values-driven shoppers. Responsive to clean-ingredient, sustainability, and wellness claims.

reasons.label: Shopped by The Wellness Optimizer, The Affluent Classic

publishers.rationale: While this highly eco-conscious audience values sustainability, they are primarily on this site to purchase organic groceries rather than apparel.
publishers.concern: A severe contextual mismatch may lead to low direct conversion rates for high-end fashion.

bidding.rationale: Start on CPM bids for 14 days to buy reach and collect conversion data (there is no history yet), then switch to a target CPA once each publisher has ~30 conversions.

creativeRotation.strategy: Even rotation for 14 days, then shift weight to the best CTR per publisher.

assumptions: No budget given: assumed $10,000 for a 30-day test.
CPMs are estimated from each audience's income tier (+15% for audiences under 5M monthly impressions); real prices come from the auction.
One-time purchase: target CPA = 30% of order value as a margin-safe default.
No publisher gets more than 25% of its monthly impressions, so no single audience is saturated.
Assumed a typical single order value of approximately $90 USD based on being positioned between Lululemon and Girlfriend Collective.
Assumed a standard one-time e-commerce purchase model.

output.understanding: The advertiser sells premium, sustainable women's activewear made from recycled ocean plastics, targeting eco-conscious and active women who value high-performance apparel.

publishers.rationale: Movewell is the perfect ecosystem for this campaign, with a heavy female audience skew (82%), a high-intent focus on activewear, and fitness-engaged shoppers who cross-shop premium wellness brands.

Stride & Stem targets high-income professional women who actively look for sustainable apparel. Their audience strongly values premium, eco-certified claims, fitting the brand's mid-to-high price point.
Cloudfoot caters to tech and urban professionals with a dedicated focus on comfort and sustainability. They command a higher AOV, making their users receptive to the premium price tier.

excluded.reason: Swiftcart is focused on quick convenience, grocery, and impulse purchases, which does not match a premium apparel buying cycle.
Studiogrid is an appointment-based service directory for fitness and spa classes, rather than a strong physical product discovery channel.
Marlowe & Co. has an older age skew (45-65) focused on workwear and casual apparel rather than sustainable activewear.
Linden Park targets conservative, older demographics focused on classic apparel and workwear, mismatched with the sporty, modern activewear style.
Everbody focuses primarily on plus-size workwear and intimates rather than dedicated sustainable athletic performance apparel.
Pawline is a pet subscription and food publisher and is entirely out of category.
Pantrygood is organic groceries and subscription boxes; while sustainable, it is not optimized for high-end fashion apparel.
Ruffco is a pet pharmacy and food marketplace with no apparel context.
Heartfoot specializes in socks, underwear, and gifting, which yields lower relevance for premium performance athletic wear.
Northbed focuses exclusively on home goods, bedding, and bath textiles.
Daily Form targets science-forward vitamins and supplements rather than sustainable apparel.
Velvetline targets Gen-Z beauty and skincare which has a lower AOV and less relevance to high-performance activewear.
Hearthstone Goods is focused strictly on cookware and non-toxic kitchenware.
Kitchenly is a meal kit delivery service and is not suitable for apparel marketing.
Tailcrate is a pet toy and subscription service, out of the athletic apparel vertical.
Strandlab is a personalized haircare beauty service and is not contextually relevant.
Pop & Sip is a functional beverage publisher and does not command the high-AOV focus of premium fashion.
